prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 3 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 2 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same moment's world, painted together: the same people, props, weather, light and colour grade in every panel.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Colombo roadside; image 2 is the reference sheet for phone; image 3 is the approved last panel of the previous part of this scene's board. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: phone exactly as shown; image 3: panel 1 of this sheet, repeated exactly: the same camera, place, light and mannequins.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Kasun is the red mannequin; Anudi is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): One painted storyboard image, four columns by three rows, read left to right and then downward: eleven panels with narrow gutters and an empty bottom-right cell. No lettering, numbers, captions or arrows appear anywhere. The surroundings and props are realistic. Soft overcast morning daylight, approximately 5600K, falls from the open road at camera right onto rain-wet concrete and patched asphalt, with muted greys, earth tones and controlled reflections. A small amber shop practical glows beneath an awning. Anudi's open navy umbrella remains in her left hand, with her structured tan handbag hanging from her left shoulder. Her orange smartphone has a transparent cover and the reference's triple-camera arrangement. The modest grey-green food three-wheeler has a dark canopy, a metal serving counter and covered food trays.

Geography: The road occupies the foreground, with the open kerb drain and narrow pavement running horizontally across the image. The food-business zone is screen left, backed by shuttered commercial frontage and a modest concrete building; the conversation takes place immediately to its right. Kasun stands left of Anudi, with the three-wheeler behind and to his left. A stained pale boundary wall stands behind Anudi and continues along the departure pavement toward screen right, ending near a utility pole visible in the widest frame. All cameras remain roadward of the Kasun–Anudi axis. Close views retain the canopy toward frame left or the pale wall toward frame right. The eventual paths run right along the wall for Anudi and left toward the serving counter for Kasun; the opening frames remain at the conversation spot.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Same roadward position and standing height as shots 1 and 3; 50mm feel, waist-up two-shot. Background: The softly resolved three-wheeler canopy remains frame left behind Kasun; the stained pale wall remains frame right behind Anudi. Kasun stands screen left with his chest facing right, head turned three-quarter right toward Anudi, and both empty hands lowered. Anudi stands screen right with her chest facing left and the phone held against the right side of her head by her raised right hand. Her head remains angled three-quarter left, while her left hand holds the umbrella shaft and the handbag stays at her left hip.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Same roadward position and standing height as shot 9; 50mm feel, waist-up two-shot. Background: The canopy and serving counter remain softly visible at frame left; the pale boundary wall remains at frame right. Kasun stands screen left with his chest facing right, his head inclined slightly toward Anudi, and both empty hands down. Anudi stands screen right with her chest facing left and her head turned three-quarter left toward him, her right elbow close to her body and the phone lowered vertically to waist level. Her left hand holds the open umbrella shaft, and the handbag remains supported by its shoulder strap.
PANEL 3 (row 2, column 1) — Roadward wide-master position aligned with shot 2, looking across the kerb drain; standing head height, 35mm feel, full figures and surrounding pavement. Background: The complete three-wheeler and shuttered frontage occupy frame left; the same pale wall continues along the open pavement to frame right, with a utility pole near the right edge. Wet asphalt and the horizontal kerb drain occupy the foreground. Kasun stands full figure screen left beside the business, chest facing right and head turned toward Anudi, with both empty hands lowered. Anudi stands full figure screen right, chest and head still directed left toward him, holding her phone at her waist in her right hand and the open umbrella in her left. Her handbag hangs at her left hip, and an unobstructed stretch of pavement extends horizontally beyond her toward screen right.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
